_comment: Mid-tier case study (4 conversations touching the ruling). Built the same way as case_study_decisions_0017.json.
ruling_title_in_decisions_md: Knowledge documents are a first-class governance artefact with their own shape, not malformed ADRs
census_method: scan_all_decisions.py --root against the 2026-08-18 backup; 0026 hit 4 conversations, 110 mentions total (the vast majority in one conversation -- see note)

timeline.event: the ruling's origin phrase, attributed to the user's own words
timeline.speaker: user
timeline.quoted_substring: "Knowledge is a decision that was made" produced 0026. "Local only" produced 0025 and 0027.
timeline.note: This line retrospectively credits the ruling's core insight to a specific user phrase -- 0026, 0025 and 0027 are described together as three rulings that all trace back to short reframings the user made in his own words.

timeline.event: drafted with grounding measurements from both estates
timeline.speaker: assistant
timeline.quoted_substring: 0026 drafted, with the real measurements from both estates in the context so it can't be r[eopened casually / disputed later]
timeline.note: This precedes seq 1 by about 2 hours and is in a DIFFERENT conversation -- so the drafting happened in local_e9841a20, and the retrospective attribution of its origin phrase happened later the same evening in local_3aee1905.

timeline.event: committed to the log and immediately used to drive a real code change
timeline.speaker: assistant
timeline.note: Same conversation and timestamp bucket as seq 2 -- drafting and ratifying happened in the same short window, unlike 0017's multi-day gap between draft and ratification.

timeline.event: the ruling exercised in a scanner change the same day
timeline.speaker: assistant
timeline.quoted_substring: git commit -m "doc_census: provenance tier + type classification, coverage grid (0026)
timeline.note: A different conversation from seq 2/3, about an hour later the same evening -- 0026 goes from ratified text to a shipped scanner change (`doc_census.py`) within hours.

timeline.event: referenced in a retrospective audit alongside its sibling rulings
timeline.speaker: assistant
timeline.quoted_substring: the three-tier registry (0012), estate-scoped visibility (0025), knowledge documents (0026), render-time reads (002[7])
timeline.note: Five days later, 0026 appears in a list of rulings being checked against ARCHITECTURE.md's staleness -- confirming it as one of the 'live' rulings a stale doc should have but doesn't.

timeline.event: cited nearly two weeks later as the precedent that justifies documenting governance rationale generally
timeline.speaker: assistant
timeline.quoted_substring: the reasoning behind 37 decisions and a dozen investigations is exactly the non-derivable material 0026 made first-class.
timeline.note: 13 days after drafting -- another 'ruling reused as precedent for a new proposal' moment, structurally similar to 0018's seq 6.

cross_check_against_decisions_md.decisions_md_states: Knowledge documents are a first-class governance artefact with their own shape, not malformed ADRs
cross_check_against_decisions_md.transcript_evidence: Consistent -- the transcript's own description ('knowledge is a decision that was made') matches DECISIONS.md's framing directly. No contradiction found.
cross_check_against_decisions_md.caveat: 80 of the 110 raw mentions are inside ONE conversation (local_3aee1905, seq 1 and 5's source) as part of a long retrospective discussion that touches many rulings at once (0012, 0025, 0026, 0027 together repeatedly) -- raw mention count here overstates how much of the STORY is cross-conversation. The n_conversations=4 signal is the more honest volume measure, per this folder's README.

why_this_is_a_good_benchmark_item: It shows a MUCH tighter draft-to-ratification-to-shipped-code loop than 0017 (hours, not days) -- a good contrast case for timing questions.

It has a real 'credited origin phrase' (seq 1) that a shallow read of only the ratification conversation (seq 2/3) would miss entirely -- testing whether a model finds attribution evidence that isn't co-located with the drafting itself.

Its high raw mention count is mostly boilerplate co-mention with sibling rulings in one retrospective conversation, not independent discussion -- a good test of whether a model's synthesis distinguishes genuine narrative beats from a ruling simply appearing in a list.
